title: Sri Kalyani Cottons — Operations & Trading Improvement
summary: Operations and trading work at a family-owned cotton manufacturing and trading business: understanding what customers actually needed, organizing inventory around quality, and finding the bottlenecks that were holding back production.
problem: In cotton trading, 'do you have what I need?' is really a question about quality — staple length, micronaire, strength, cleanliness, moisture — and a customer's needs rarely map cleanly to a single lot on hand. Meanwhile, production had bottlenecks that were quietly capping throughput. Both problems came down to understanding the operation and the customer well enough to make a good call.
approach: Worked directly with customers to understand the cotton quality and specifications they needed, and supported trade decisions against that. On the production side, I analyzed the workflow, identified bottlenecks, monitored operations, and helped drive process improvements. A practical shift: thinking about inventory in terms of its quality parameters, so the team could find lots that matched a customer's need — or discuss a workable alternative — instead of simply saying inventory wasn't available.
outcome: Process changes I contributed to were part of a roughly 25% increase in production throughput, and reframing inventory around quality parameters helped turn dead-end 'not available' conversations into matches or workable alternatives for customers.
